Subject: Official run results (2026-11-08) — preliminary

Team — attached is the preliminary results CSV (run-20261108-summary.csv) and a short summary:

- Run configuration: 4-hour sustained window, ramp to 8 clients per worker, 15 workers, prompt mix matched to production token distribution.
- P95 latency (end-to-end): 208 ms (slightly above MAP baseline of 200 ms)
- TTFT median: 46 ms; TTFT P95: 67 ms (above 50 ms target)
- Sustained throughput: 610 tokens/sec (meets throughput target)
- Peak concurrency observed: 132 concurrent requests during burst (exceeded 120 target)
- Error rate: 1.6% (missed <1% error budget; majority were transient 429s during bursts)
- GPU utilization: sustained 78% on the dedicated pool; kernel-level metrics indicate <10% serialization overhead.

Observations / quick corrective items:
1) TTFT P95 is elevated during bursty periods — likely due to small cold-cache spikes and connection pool limits.
2) Transient 429s correlate with short-lived concurrency spikes; recommend raising per-instance connection pool and enabling short-lived fallback to a slightly lower-cost model variant during spikes.
3) P95 miss (208 ms) is borderline — may be improved by tuning batching and increasing prefetch worker threads.

Recommended follow-ups (mapped to MAP actions):
- Immediate: Increase connection pool + adjust load balancer timeout (Diego/Platform).
- 48-hour: Re-run a focused 2-hour window with adjusted pool sizes and incremental quantization profile (Marissa/Karthik).
- Decision: If P95 remains >200 ms after two focused re-runs, propose a short Dedicated capacity increase (add 2 A10G-equivalent nodes) as an MAP escalation item.

Renee — please confirm whether Acme will accept the proposed follow-ups in the MAP and whether you want us to open a short SLA exception for burst protection while you finalize firewall rules.

Thanks,
Karthik
